decisions.executionNote: Begin a continuous elbow-up right-arm approach to the set square; gently tilt the gripper downward while keeping clear of cubes.
Reduce the initial approach increments after the continuity rejection; retain the observed configuration.
Continue right-arm approach above the right half of the set square, pitching the fingers toward the table with small joint-continuous steps.
Move above the tool's right end and continue pitching downward; keep the left arm at its reset pose.
Complete most of the downward pitch above the tool; maintain clearance before orienting the jaws across its narrow width.
Bring the gripper nearly vertical with a slight clearance lift before yawing across the set square.
Yaw the open right gripper toward a crosswise grasp of the tool while centering over its right portion.
Continue yaw alignment above the bar without touching the cubes.
Finish the crosswise jaw orientation and begin a cautious vertical descent over the right end of the set square.
Seat the fingers a few millimeters around the tool and close for a tabletop grasp; visual retention remains to be checked.
Hold the tabletop pose and allow the closing command to settle before testing tool engagement.
Test retention by slowly rotating the set square in the tabletop plane toward a straight transverse edge; keep the grasp closed.
The bar follows the gripper. Fine-straighten its edge and advance gently toward the blocks, keeping the tool low and the cubes on the table.
Advance the nearly horizontal straightedge toward the staggered block faces with a small yaw correction; maintain tabletop height.
Bring the straightedge closer to the nearest cube while removing the remaining small edge skew. No vertical cube manipulation.
Push slowly through the stagger with the straightedge, allowing each cube to settle against the same face while maintaining height.
Make a final gentle seating push and tiny straightness correction; all three cubes now appear face-aligned and remain on the table.
Withdraw the held straightedge horizontally from the aligned row without lifting or disturbing any cube, preparing to set it down and reset.
Release the set square at its current low position, clear of the cube faces, before retracting the empty right arm.
Lift only the empty gripper away from the released tool and begin reversing its yaw toward the reset configuration; preserve the aligned blocks.
Retract within the right workspace while unwinding the gripper yaw along the continuous elbow-up return path.
Continue the empty-arm return, unwinding yaw above the clear tabletop and leaving the aligned cubes undisturbed.
Finish unwinding yaw and begin restoring the original gripper pitch while retracting along the previously cleared path.
Restore the right arm toward its original position and pitch in small continuous steps, keeping the elbow-up branch.
Continue reversing the approach toward the reset pose, reducing pitch and retracting without contacting the tool or aligned row.
Slow the final approach to the original pose, preserving joint continuity as the right arm nears its reset configuration.
